extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters, regulatory attorneys, environmental advocates, and commenters on MACT/NESHAP rulemakings
extracted.subtask_short: MACT review for oil and gas
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and prescribe how EPA must calculate and update MACT floors and beyond-the-floor standards for oil and gas source categories (glycol dehydrators, storage vessels, equipment leaks), including data sufficiency, numeric limits per HAP, and incorporation of recent control technologies and LDAR practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floors must be based on performance of the best sources with emissions data
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112(d) states that MACT floors must be based on the performance of the best sources for which the Administrator has emissions data; EPA must determine whether the available data (e.g., 2005 data) are sufficient for setting MACT floors and, if not, collect emission test data to recalculate proper MACT floors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legacy data are unreliable or unrepresentative, EPA must collect new emission test data; cannot rely on simple judgment calls or assign efficiencies based on chosen control technology when actual top-performer data exist. (See discussion on 1997/1999 survey deficiencies and need to recalculate floors.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate MACT floors with substantial evidence (no regard to cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy the 'floor' requirement, EPA must 'demonstrate with substantial evidence - not mere assertions' that the chosen floors represent 'a reasonable estimate of the performance of the [best-performing] units.' The MACT 'floor' must be determined 'without regard to costs or other factors' listed in §112(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support floors with actual performance data from best-performing similar sources; use statutory tests and case law (e.g., Ne. Md., Nat'l Lime) to justify the selection and representativeness of the sample used to set the floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct beyond-the-floor analysis only after correct floor determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112(d)(2) requires EPA to perform a beyond-the-floor analysis—determining whether limitations more stringent than the MACT floor are achievable—only after the MACT floor has been properly determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond-the-floor analysis must consider cost of achieving reductions, non-air quality health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements. Absent an up-to-date floor analysis based on current controls, a meaningful beyond-the-floor determination cannot be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set numeric limits for each HAP (no aggregation as single percent reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 112(d)(6) and 112(d)(3) require EPA to set a numeric limit for each HAP emitted by the source category. It is unlawful and arbitrary to require a single aggregated percent reduction (e.g., 'reduce all HAP emissions by 95 percent') in place of numeric limits for each HAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must set emission standards for each listed HAP emitted (e.g., BTEX and other individual HAPs), and may express such standards in units like pounds per unit of throughput (lb/MMScf). Reliance on an overall control technology percentage is insufficient absent evidence it achieves required reductions for each HAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalculate MACT floor for large glycol dehydrators using current best-performer data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must update the MACT floor and consider setting a beyond-the-floor standard for large glycol dehydrators by calculating the floor for each HAP emitted, reflecting the emissions levels of the most efficient performers, not relying on the flawed 1997 survey or the 1999 judgmental 95% assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve information gaps in the record, consider control efficiencies achieved in practice (e.g., up to 99%), and ensure standards reflect performance achieved today. Do not carry forward unsupported conclusions from prior rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalculate MACT floor and new-source limits for storage vessels with potential for flash emissions (PFE)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must identify best-performing existing sources (top 12% or best 5 when <30 sources) and calculate both existing- and new-source MACT floors and limits for tanks with flash potential, including units previously unregulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on 1997 survey results if they are unrepresentative; separately examine appropriate new-source MACT floors and limits for flash-potential tanks, and ensure the rule covers the entire universe of storage vessel units that contribute major HAP emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT for equipment leaks must reflect best-performing facilities and not the worst-expected performance
rubrics_metrics.description: In establishing MACT for equipment leaks, EPA must identify the top-performing facilities and base floors on their achieved performance rather than adopting the worst-expected performance or simply transplanting NSPS work-practice artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider more stringent programs (e.g., California), and ensure exemptions or monitoring deferrals are evaluated for their emissions and public health impacts. The new-source MACT floor should be at least as stringent as the most stringent comparable programs in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify work-practice standards under §112(h)(4) if not using numeric limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA continues to use only a work-practice standard for equipment leaks, it must explain why that approach is lawful under section 112(h)(4), which generally requires a numeric standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legal and evidentiary support for substituting work-practice standards for numeric emission limits; absent such justification, numeric limits are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not import NSPS exemptions/deferred repair options into MACT without evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions and deferrals carried from NSPS (e.g., exemptions for unsafe/difficult monitoring, deferral if repair requires shutdown, option for more frequent monitoring in exchange for a permanent 2% leak rate) cannot be adopted for MACT floors without analyzing impacts and comparing to best performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify the impact of these exemptions on HAP emissions and public health; remove or limit such exemptions where they are inconsistent with MACT's reliance on best-performing facilities. Do not allow permanent 2% leak rate tradeoffs without caps or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use up-to-date evaluation of LDAR practices and set detection thresholds consistent with best performers
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must conduct a comprehensive evaluation of LDAR practices in the sector, determine whether proposed thresholds (e.g., 500 ppm vs 10,000 ppm) represent the MACT floor, and base MACT on best-performing programs (e.g., BAAQMD, California jurisdictions) where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review compliance reports to identify sources with lowest leak levels and fewest unrepairable leaks. Adopt lower detection thresholds if they reflect best practice, and ensure LDAR practices represent the floor for both new and existing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: LDAR programs must include all components in hydrocarbon service and avoid percentage-based HAP exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions for components contacting streams with <5% or <10% HAP (or VOC) are cost-based and must not be imported into MACT floor determinations without quantifying health impacts; LDAR should cover all hydrocarbon-service components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BAAQMD and other programs that do not provide these exemptions demonstrate feasibility; EPA must not permit sources to choose the least effective requirements among applicable programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require advanced/zero-emissions technologies and leakless designs for new sources when demonstrated by best performers
rubrics_metrics.description: New sources must employ advanced 'zero emissions' technologies where technically feasible and as demonstrated by best-performing sources; require leakless valve technology improvements and higher percentages of leakless devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exempt new compressors at the wellhead from best-seal technology requirements. Limit 'nonrepairable' exemptions for new sources to failures of leakless-design components only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition monitoring deferrals on equipment replacement at next turnaround and restrict deferred repair limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring deferrals at existing facilities should be conditioned on replacement with leakless technology at the next turnaround (not to exceed a specified period), and gross emitters must not be allowed to defer until turnaround. Allowable deferrals must be restricted to components that leak below specified limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: deferrals tied to turnaround, not exceed five years; restrict deferral eligibility; do not permit continued emissions by gross emitters while awaiting turnaround.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace frequently-failing components with upgraded technology (component-replacement threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: MACT should require replacing components with upgraded technology if the number of leaks within a specified time period exceeds a rule-specified threshold (e.g., SCAQMD/Ventura rules: replace components with >5 major leaks in a year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit thresholds and remediation options (e.g., replace with bellows-seal or other BACT/BARCT technologies or route to approved control devices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent auditing and oversight of LDAR programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Given historical underreporting and enforcement problems, MACT should include independent auditing of LDAR activities for large sources (e.g., once every five years) and alternative industry-sponsored random audits for smaller sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audits to guard against underreporting and ensure LDAR effectiveness; tailor frequency/coverage by source size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use remote/optical/ultrasound/infrared scanning as complementary screening tools, not substitutes for LDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Optical scanning, ultrasound, and infrared cameras can be part of an improved LDAR program to find gross emitters and target inspections, but currently cannot replace LDAR for quantifying emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ remote scans for daily/weekly screening to identify problem areas; use Method 21 and other methods for quantification where necessary. Evaluate Smart LDAR IR cameras and other tech but do not assume equivalence without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate detection devices to methane and track methane as part of LDAR for HAP control
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibration of Method 21 monitors with methane and tracking methane concentrations enhances the ability to detect organic HAP leaks (because methane is the dominant stream), and programs that track methane (e.g., BAAQMD) demonstrate feasibility and should inform MACT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider calibration procedures, thresholds, and the practice of monitoring methane as a proxy to detect and repair HAP leaks more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and adopt advances in control technologies for glycol dehydrators
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must consider oxidation units (flares/thermal incinerators with 98–99% destruction), condensers used with flash tanks and combustion units, zero-emissions dehydrators, and desiccant dehydrators as feasible control options achieving significantly greater HAP reductions than existing/proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look to state programs (e.g., Wyoming, Texas) requiring 98–100% control and to EPA Gas Star documentation; evaluate combinations of condensers + combustion, enclosed smokeless combustion, and replacement technologies when determining floors and beyond-the-floor options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider technology advances for storage vessels including vapor recovery and recompression systems
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must evaluate vapor recovery units, reconsider floating roof applicability for certain liquids, assess thermal/catalytic oxidizers and combustion devices, and consider systems that capture vented vapors and recompress them into saleable product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RBLC database, Natural Gas Star partners, and state jurisdiction experience to assess performance and to justify updated MACT levels (examples include systems achieving ≥98% reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on legacy (pre-1997) data when higher-quality recent data are available
rubrics_metrics.description: Where recent actual emissions data of higher quality are readily available (e.g., 2005 NEI), using legacy data that fail to reflect industry developments for calculating numeric standards at the floor or beyond-the-floor stages is arbitrary and capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must show how legacy datasets are representative of current operations if it continues to rely on them; otherwise, it must update analyses using current, comprehensive data to determine floors and beyond-the-floor measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate MACT floors for small glycol dehydrators consistent with §112(d)(2)-(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For small glycol dehydrators (specific flowrate and benzene emission cutoffs), EPA must set existing-source and new-source MACT floors based on the average of the best performing 12% (or best 5 if <30) for existing sources and the performance achieved in practice by the best controlled similar source for new sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure unit-specific numeric limits (e.g., BTEX limits proposed) are based on up-to-date representative data and not solely on pre-1997 surveys. Where better data exist, recalculation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine MACT floors for all HAPs emitted by small glycols and other subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must determine and set MACT floor standards for each HAP emitted by small glycol dehydrators (and other subcategories), rather than limiting standards to a subset of HAPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid singling out only BTEX; provide standards and analyses for all listed HAPs emitted by the sources to meet the statutory obligation to set emission standards for each listed HAP.
